citation.title: Analytical approximation of cross-section effects on charge exchange spectra observed in hot fusion plasmas
citation.authors: M von Hellermann, P Breger, J Frieling, R König, W Mandl, A Maas, H P Summers

topic: Collision-energy-dependent CX emission-rate effects on apparent impurity temperature, velocity and intensity in Gaussian-fitted CES spectra (JET)
own_question: Can cross-section effects on thermal CX spectra be approximated analytically and inverted to recover true Ti, rotation and intensity?
actual_method_and_evidence: Fits a parametric emission-rate function and approximates it as an exponential with linear and quadratic terms, giving closed-form apparent width, shift and averaged rate, plus an algebraic inversion. Compares these with numerical velocity-space integration for C VI, He II and Be IV. Applies the method to JET pulses with D, T and He beams. The analytical-numerical agreement degrades for He II above about 10 keV.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Reported CES impurity temperatures come from model-dependent spectral fitting. Beam-energy-dependent CX cross sections can shift apparent temperature and velocity relative to the underlying distribution, so CES reports are conventional labels rather than direct physical truth.
claim_checks.qualification: Demonstrated for JET geometry and beams at high Ti. The size of the effect for KSTAR pedestal-top carbon CES is unknown.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Standard CES analysis assumes a Gaussian Doppler profile. That assumption can weaken when ion thermal velocities approach beam velocities.
claim_checks.qualification: This is the authors' interpretation, based on analytical-numerical divergence for He II. It is not a general accuracy bound.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Offline spectral correction only. No timing, latency, nowcasting or BES/ECEI content.
validation_if_relevant: Analytical versus numerical model comparison, plus JET data examples. No held-out data and no independent Ti truth.
forbidden_inferences: That KSTAR CES labels carry a specific bias magnitude
That this work involves real-time or causal estimation
Generalizing JET high-Ti results to pedestal-top conditions
Treating the corrected values as independent physical truth
Using it to motivate a new correction method in our study
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Supports the background framing that CES temperatures are processed, model-dependent impurity Ti labels. It is useful context for not calling labels truth, and is not a method we implement.
